title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: PDMRs
tiers.description: Persons Discharging Managerial Responsibilities: any Director or senior executive of the Company who has regular access to Inside Information and the power to make managerial decisions affecting the Company's future developments and business prospects, as determined by the Company.

tiers.name: Applicable Employee
tiers.description: An Employee who is likely to be in possession of Inside Information in relation to the Company irrespective of his or her holding or interest in the Company. Subject to the same Closed Period, clearance, derivatives/hedging and margin lending restrictions as PDMRs, but not the PDMR-specific notification and disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any employee or consultant of the Company who is not a PDMR or Applicable Employee. May Deal in Company Securities at any time, including during what would otherwise be a Closed Period, provided they do not possess Inside Information; not subject to the derivatives/hedging ban, margin lending ban, Closed Periods or clearance procedure.

tiers.name: PCAs
tiers.description: Persons closely associated with a PDMR: a spouse or equivalent partner; a dependent child or stepchild under 18; a relative sharing the same household as the PDMR for at least one year; or a legal person, trust or partnership whose managerial responsibilities are discharged by, controlled by, set up for the benefit of, or economically equivalent to, the PDMR or those persons.

rules.detail: Absolute, all-times ban (not limited to Closed Periods) on dealing in any financial product issued or created over or in respect of Company Securities, expressly including hedge arrangements. The only carve-out is an option over unissued capital granted by the Company (i.e. an employee/director option), not a bank-written OTC derivative.

For the avoidance of doubt this clause does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. A short sale is a disposal under the general 'Deal' definition (not a 'financial product created over' the Securities), so it is subject to the ordinary 2-Business-Day prior clearance regime and the Closed Period ban, and, if motivated by short-term considerations, would also breach clause 13's speculative dealing ban.
rules.evidence: A PDMRs may not deal in Company Securities on considerations of a short term nature.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

A CFD referencing Company Securities is a 'financial product ... created over or in respect of' the Securities (the FCA notification form in Schedule 8 explicitly lists 'a contract for difference' as an example transaction type), so it falls within the same absolute, all-times ban as hedge arrangements.

financing_disclosure: PDMRs; trigger: appointment (initial disclosure), any change (ongoing disclosure), and ceasing to be a PDMR (final disclosure); to: Company Secretary, and via lodgement to ASX/AIM/the FCA; deadline: 2 Business Days for initial/final disclosure, 1 Business Day for ongoing changes; covers 'all contracts ... that confer a right to call for or deliver shares' in the Company, which would include put/call contracts with a bank.

exemption_authority: The Approving Officer may grant clearance to sell (not buy) during a Closed Period only in Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, or an unforeseen circumstance the Board considers consistent with the Policy's objectives), limited to the number of shares needed to obtain the required funds, only if there is no Inside Information, and (if applicable) only with AIM permission where the PDMR is subject to an AIM Rule 7 lock-in agreement. Bulk clearance may also be granted without individual application for dealings connected with employee share plans.
jurisdiction_overlays: EU Market Abuse Regulation (596/2014) as applied in the UK ('MAR')
AIM Rules for Companies (London Stock Exchange)
UK FCA notification requirements for PDMR/PCA dealings over EUR5,000

bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs or Applicable Employees are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements). For the avoidance of doubt this clause does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies that merely require clearance for a derivative, SVM bans PDMRs and Applicable Employees from any financial product created over the shares at all times, including outside Closed Periods; a bank-written put and call collar is squarely caught and there is no clearance route to permit it — the only listed carve-out is a Company-granted employee option, not a third-party derivative.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs or Applicable Employees are prohibited at all times from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is banned outright and permanently, not just during Closed Periods, and the 'similar arrangements' language is broad enough to catch most secured-lending structures against the shares, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances override in this section.

bespoke_clauses.clause: details of all contracts (other than contracts to which the Company is a party) to which the PDMR is a party or under which the PDMR is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in ... the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if a collar or financing arrangement were otherwise permissible, the put/call contracts with the bank would likely need to be disclosed to the Company Secretary as PDMR disclosures under Schedule 5 and reported to ASX/AIM/the FCA, increasing transparency and timing constraints around any such structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under MAR, dealings in Company securities over EUR5,000 within a calendar year by PDMRs or a PCA must be notified promptly, and in any event within three (3) business days, on AIM and to the FCA through its website.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any dealing that were somehow permitted would trigger public MAR disclosure of the transaction to the market within 3 business days, and a UK AIM Rule 7 lock-in agreement (if any) could independently block Closed Period sale clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Closed Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy has no separate unvested/holding-locked share category for hedging purposes; the section 6.3 and 6.4 bans apply identically 'at all times' regardless of vesting status, so there is no window where hedging or financing becomes available merely because shares have vested.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable under this policy for either PDMRs or Applicable Employees. Section 6.3 bans them, at all times (not just during Closed Periods), from dealing in any financial product issued or created over or in respect of Company Securities, expressly including hedge arrangements, with the only carve-out being a Company-granted option over unissued capital, so the purchased put and written call legs of a collar are prohibited outright with no clearance route. Section 6.4 separately and absolutely bans PDMRs and Applicable Employees from margin lending or 'similar arrangements' in respect of Company Securities they hold or have a Relevant Interest in, at all times, so the loan leg is equally prohibited. Ordinary Employees who are neither PDMRs nor Applicable Employees are not named in either ban and may deal, including in derivatives, subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the ordinary clearance and Closed Period regime, but they are unlikely to be the audience for a bank-funded collar. Even a permitted financing contract would trigger PDMR contract-disclosure obligations under Schedule 5 and, if a dealing did occur, MAR notification to AIM and the FCA within three business days.
